classifier_rationale: The caller raised two separate issues in one call: a duplicate $220.00 Harvest Table Market charge (WA) and an undelivered $145.00 Trailhead Gear backpack (NR).

retrieved.text: Fraud routing. Any charge the cardholder says they didn't make or authorize goes to the fraud team on the same call. Block the card, reissue, open a fraud claim. Agents do not open these as billing disputes only.

The 60-day window. The issuer must receive the notice within 60 days after it sent the first statement showing the error. If a statement wasn't sent, the clock runs from when it should have been. For a missing credit, it runs from the statement where the credit should have appeared.

Quality disputes (claims and defenses). A complaint about the quality of goods the cardholder accepted isn't a billing error. It may qualify as a claim against the issuer if the cardholder tried in good faith to resolve it with the merchant, the purchase was over $50, and it happened in the cardholder's state or within 100 miles of their address. The $50 and location limits don't apply when the merchant and issuer are related.

note: Cardholder Leon Abernathy reported two issues. (1) Harvest Table Market: a $220 charge dated 2026-09-12 posted twice for one checkout. Cardholder called the store manager twice and got no callback. (2) Trailhead Gear: a $145 daypack ordered 2026-09-12 never arrived. Tracking stopped updating, and two messages through the website contact form got no reply. Statement date not stated, so the 60-day window is unknown. No dispute opened. Written notice to the issuer not mentioned. Escalated to supervisor due to low-confidence intent. Supervisor to confirm whether the Harvest charge is a duplicate billing error and how to handle the Trailhead non-delivery under the claims path (REG-13). Unknown: statement date, whether Trailhead is related to the issuer, delivery status beyond the tracking history.
